definition: Decides whether the original base layers of the EfficientNetB0 model are allowed to update during training.
impact: Keeping these layers frozen preserves the general image recognition patterns the model learned from ImageNet. Unfreezing them allows the model to fine-tune those patterns specifically for birds.

definition: Decides whether the middle layers of the model are allowed to update during training.
impact: Freezing these layers keeps their learned patterns stable while the top layers adapt. Unfreezing them gives the model more flexibility to adjust how it processes images.

definition: Decides whether the final layers of the model (closest to the output) are allowed to update during training.
impact: Freezing these layers locks in existing predictions. Unfreezing them allows the model to change how it maps image features to bird species.

definition: Controls how much the model adjusts its internal settings after each training batch.
impact: A high learning rate learns faster but can overshoot and become unstable. A low learning rate makes smaller, more careful adjustments and is more stable but slower to converge.

definition: Randomly disables a percentage of neurons during each training step.
impact: Prevents the model from relying too heavily on any one neuron, which reduces overfitting and helps it generalize to images it has never seen before.

definition: The number of times the model goes through the entire training dataset from start to finish.
impact: More epochs give the model more chances to learn patterns, but too many can cause it to memorize the training data rather than learning to generalize.

definition: The number of training images the model processes at one time before updating its weights.
impact: Larger batches are faster to train but require more memory. Smaller batches use less memory and can sometimes help the model generalize better.

definition: The algorithm the model uses to adjust its internal weights after each training batch.
impact: Different optimizers (such as Adam or SGD) affect how quickly the model learns and how stable the training process is.
